title: P31 domain constitution
description: The machine-readable contract every governed domain declares. Conforming to this schema is what makes a domain governable by @p31ca/govern. The structure is identical across design, monetization, justice, and any future domain; only the content changes. A constitution that does not validate is not a constitution — it is a hand-edited mirror.

schema.description: Version-in-URI. When the schema changes, the URI changes, and constitutions migrate explicitly. There is no separate version field to drift from the URI.

version.description: The constitution's own version. Distinct from the schema version — a domain's constitution evolves independently of the schema it conforms to.

genesisTimestamp.description: The moment governance began for this domain. The domain's Genesis Gate. Without it, there is no way to answer 'how long has this been governed?'

resolutionRoot.description: Optional. The directory (relative to the constitution's own directory) that runbook and mirror paths resolve against. Defaults to the constitution's own directory (constitutionRoot). Lets a domain point at runbooks that live in a sibling repo or a shared library without copying them. Additive-optional — constitutions without it are unaffected.

mirrors.description: Every artifact that claims to represent the canonical source. A mirror without a parityGate is an unchecked claim.

remediation.description: A pointer to the runbook that tells you how to fix the failure. A gate whose remediation is 'fix it' has zero information content.

expected.description: The strong contract the runtime enforces: the negative control must exit 0 AND emit the literal NEGATIVE_CONTROL_OK marker. Exit 0 without the marker = the control did nothing (furniture). Exit non-zero = the control is broken. A gate whose negative control cannot prove it fails is furniture.

prevention.description: Must resolve to a real runbook id or a gate id. A sentiment is not a prevention.

who.description: BLOCKING domains require the four-party K4 topology (User, Issuer, Ledger, Court). OBSERVATIONAL domains may declare a single review credential during bootstrapping. The Scutum Fidei argument: only four vertices guarantee co-equality; three collapses to K3 (planar, no enclosed volume); two is a line; one is a point.

abdication.description: The review cadence's terminal state. Paper XXV: 'if it requires the creator to maintain it, it has failed.' After N clean cycles, the domain transitions to ABDICATED — self-governing. The transition requires explicit human sign-off (the Centaur boundary: the runtime does the work, the human retains final authority).

chainName.description: A domain may name its chain 'genesis' to match Paper XII's Genesis Block contract. The runtime stays generic; the constitution names the chain.

aspirational.description: Claims the domain intends but does not yet enforce. Per Paper XIX: a claim without traceable OQE is aspirational, not true. Research-only claims are parked here, never silently promoted.

reference.description: Where the evidence lives: a file path, a URL, a DOI, a command that reproduces it.

oqe.description: Objective Quality Evidence. The 7 evidence classes are per Paper XIX (SOULSAFE). A claim without a traceable OQE source is aspirational.

credentialRef.description: Either a role name (during bootstrapping) or a credential array. A string is acceptable at OBSERVATIONAL; a credential array is required at BLOCKING.

fourPartyReview.description: The K4 four-party attestation: User, Issuer, Ledger, Court. The classical CBS analogue of the SIC-POVM's four measurement outcomes — the deployable primitive. (SIC-POVM itself is research-only and must never be claimed as deployed.)
